All 20 mechanisms fit the first experiment almost equally well (NLL ~-22.4 to -22.8). This indicates the baseline experiment was not discriminative — all mechanisms can fit a single clean reaction trace. This is expected for the first experiment. I need to design conditions that provoke mechanism-specific behavior.

<hypothesis>
To discriminate among the 20 mechanisms, I need to probe several key features simultaneously:
- **Product inhibition / reverse reaction** (distinguishes M12, M17 vs others): adding product initially
- **Catalyst order dependence** (distinguishes M3 which uses cat2 dimer, M2, M13, M19): varying [cat]
- **Substrate inhibition / decay** (M11, M16): high [S]
- **Deactivation over time** (M6, M8, M9, M10, M14, M20): long timescale

A single experiment can't do all of these. For this experiment, I'll focus on probing catalyst concentration dependence and deactivation. A **low catalyst** concentration with high substrate will stretch out the reaction timescale, making deactivation pathways (first-order in cat or catS) show clear stalling. This condition also helps M3 (cat2 dimer) stand out because [cat] dependence becomes nonlinear.

Using low [cat] = 0.002 M with [S] = 1.0 M will slow the reaction enough to detect stalling. No product added, to keep things clean.
</hypothesis>
